defensive_partners.name: threat intelligence provider
defensive_partners.data_and_capabilities: Full malware analysis.  Customer end-point and appliance data. Honeypots.  Customer account, email, etc. data. Customer network and end-point logs.

defensive_partners.name: cybersecurity service provider
defensive_partners.data_and_capabilities: Has insight into potential adversary activity, can secure multiple organizations through deployment of security controls, unique data sets for insight into threat activity.

defensive_partners.name: internet service provider
defensive_partners.data_and_capabilities: Netflow. ACLs. IP ownership. Route advertisements. DNS records. Visibility and monitoring of potential adversary infrastructure, can provide IOCs, and take down adversary infrastructure if necessary.

defensive_partners.name: cloud infrastructure provider
defensive_partners.data_and_capabilities: Visibility and monitoring of potential adversary infrastructure, can provide IOCs, and take down adversary infrastructure if necessary.

defensive_partners.name: hardware or software vendor
defensive_partners.data_and_capabilities: Has insight into potential adversary activity, can secure multiple organizations through deployment of security controls, unique data sets for insight into threat activity.

defensive_partners.name: industrial control system vendor
defensive_partners.data_and_capabilities: Has insight into potential adversary activity, can secure multiple organizations through deployment of security controls, unique data sets for insight into threat activity.

defensive_partners.name: national CSIRT
defensive_partners.data_and_capabilities: Log data from national government networks. Data shared from industry partners.  National intelligence and law enforcement data.

defensive_partners.name: industry- or community-led sharing organization
defensive_partners.data_and_capabilities: Unique data, reach, and trust into the center’s community of interest.

defensive_partners.name: national law enforcement
defensive_partners.data_and_capabilities: Unique intellignece insights, coordinate and execute LE disruption operations, pursue investigations and prosecutions.

defensive_partners.name: mature enterprise network owner/operator
defensive_partners.data_and_capabilities: On-the-ground detection, might be explicitly targeted by adversaries and can provide up-to-date/new IOCs helpful for other organizations to detect similar adversary activity.

defensive_partners.name: national military
defensive_partners.data_and_capabilities: Insights from offensive operations and defense of military networks. Ability to conduct offensive disruption operations.

defensive_partners.name: national intelligence community
defensive_partners.data_and_capabilities: Has insight into past and present behaviors which could be indicative of future or on-going adversary activity. Can provide context into behavior and potential backing of adversary groups.

defensive_partners.name: sector-specific authority or regulator
defensive_partners.data_and_capabilities: Insights into specific critical infrastructure sectors. Can amplify mitigation activities. May have regulatory authority to drive defensive actions.

techniques.name: Monitor
techniques.description: Upon finding an active adversary, closely monitor and track until the appropriate time for mitigation.

techniques.name: Report
techniques.description: Report sightings of the adversary to a designated coordinator.

techniques.name: Share
techniques.description: Share sightings and related indicators broadly or with a trusted group.

techniques.name: Prioritize
techniques.description: Define and communicate priorities for defense.

techniques.name: Partner
techniques.description: Identify partners needed to achieve defensive priorities.

techniques.name: Assess
techniques.description: Conduct risk assessment to identify gaps and opportunities for collaborative defense.

techniques.name: Plan
techniques.description: Develop and update collaborative or enterprise response, operational, and strategic plans.

techniques.name: Notify
techniques.description: Notify targets or victims of vulnerable systems or attempted/successful intrusions.

techniques.name: Alert
techniques.description: Release a priority alert or analysis report.

techniques.name: Brief
techniques.description: Provide briefings to industry and government leaders on the threat or incident.

techniques.name: Review
techniques.description: Conduct and share an after-action report and recommendations.

techniques.name: Deploy
techniques.description: Prioritize service deployment to targeted sectors, including incident response, hunt, assessment, or hardening services.

playbooks.name: playbook-mockup-jan-2025-monitor-priority
playbooks.description: As part of a broader collaboration effort led by ABC-CERT, this playbook provides action pathways to partners to take further action on these specific IOC’s. This playbook is specifically for Cybersecurity Service Providers, Cloud Platform Providers, and enterprise IT vendors. At this stage of the defensive campaign, partners are being asked to monitor the threat and coordinate with the CERT before mitigating activity they see on their infrastructure. This playbook helps ensure that intelligence gain/loss considerations are weighed strategically before threats are mitigated at the tactical level.

collaboration_actions.description: First, hunt for these IOC’s on your infrastructure and available data sets.

Second, upon finding indications of the adversary, report the sighting to the CERT as quickly as possible. Through continued monitoring, your organization may be able to provide valuable intelligence that can help disrupt the threat actor in a strategic way.
Third, continue to monitor the threat actor and report any new activity.  If the threat actor reaches a point where damage can occur, mitigate immediately.
